# Mars God's Eye — Mission Viewer

> NASA Space Apps 2026 project (challenge: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map; team: Houston, We Have a Bug!). The default entry is a six-zone selector with illustrative stories on real terrain. The separate recorded-recovery-002 entry replays height-recovery-20261115-01: real data/mapping/planner/recorder software, MOCK mission and kinematic human, one SIMULATED contradiction, parked/idle robots and final READY. Historical recorded-recovery-001 is preserved unchanged. Neither recording is a validated LIVE or coordinated three-agent mission. An optional ?gateway=<url> status panel is read-only and independent of the recorded 3D scene.

Mission playback is a REPLAY of simulated data, not a live mission. The public orbital inputs retain their separate observational provenance.

## What is real and what is simulated

- Featured recording: public CTX prior and recorded belief/sigma/observed versions on a 32x32 grid at 4 m, 128 m across, with 20 m native CTX source spacing and separate MGS/MOLA regional context. Resampling adds no native detail. Absolute datum and recorded poses are preserved.
- Separate illustrative Jezero demo: provisional 3.4 km x 7.6 km NASA/USGS CTX crop on an 8 m display grid, interpolated from 20 m native terrain, draped MRO CTX image (NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS/USGS, via JPL Mars Trek), and USGS SIM 3464 geology. Geology boundaries have about 100-200 m registration uncertainty and do not identify a precise sampling cell. These layers are not silently attached to the 128 m recording.
- Historical references, not live weather: Perseverance MEDA daily summaries at Jezero (a few sols) and the published MSL RAD surface dose rate at Gale (Hassler et al. 2014), used for an estimated crew dose.
- The illustrative demo's mission, routes, agent motion, budgets, scarp and POIs are generated data. The featured recording instead contains the planner's actual outputs and executed MOCK states; its budgets and observation inputs remain experimental. Vertical exaggeration is display only and is specified per run.
- The browser never plans routes: it draws the routes and decisions recorded in the replay.

## How to read the viewer

- Mode label: top right, REPLAY with the package's source (MOCK for the featured recording, SIMULATION for the generated demo; never LIVE).
- Tabs: Exploration (agents, tasks, routes), Ground layers (geologic map and schematic cut-away), Atmos (MEDA and RAD references), Mission replay (event log).
- Terrain layers: Orbital map (prior), Updated map (per recorded map version), Slope (Horn 3x3 at the current grid spacing), Uncertainty (reported model sigma). The derivative window is 12 m on the 4 m recording grid and 24 m on the 8 m demo display grid; both source and grid spacing are shown. Neither slope bands nor sigma certify passage.
- Agent dial (bottom right): oxygen, energy, time, route, atmosphere and dose gauges around a heading-up minimap.
- Cameras: Map, Astronaut, Rover, Drone, Base; V switches the followed agent between third and first person. In first person the HUD shows a compass, site bearings, the agent dial with resources and a minimap, the route ahead with the next waypoint, and resource alerts.
- Terrain scan (Q in first person): a visual pulse around the astronaut that redraws the run's prior-derived slope classes (< 8°, 8–15°, ≥ 15°) and NoData on the surface. It is not a sensor, observation or mission command; map, uncertainty and routes remain unchanged.
- Keyboard: Space play/pause, ←/→ ±5 s, Home restart, F follow the selected agent, G grab-to-drag map, Q/E rotate (Q is the terrain scan in first person), V first person, C drone camera, L helmet lights, I artificial / real light, B camera sway in first person.
- URL parameters: ?run=demo (default: the illustrative Jezero story, reached from a Mars globe selector of six zones), ?run=gale-demo, gusev-demo, insight-demo, meridiani-demo or melas-demo (the other zones, also simulated stories on real terrain), ?run=recorded-recovery-002 (height-corrected recorded MOCK recovery with a parked drone, intro omitted), ?run=recorded-recovery-001 (historical recording retained unchanged), or ?run=mock-vertical-001 (historical flat-MOCK recording); ?nointro=1 skips the demo intro. Entry folders and internal run IDs are separate identifiers.

## Machine-readable data

- Featured recording: [manifest](https://jorgefajardom-coder.github.io/NASA-GODS-EYE-/replay/recorded-recovery-001/manifest.json), [timeline](https://jorgefajardom-coder.github.io/NASA-GODS-EYE-/replay/recorded-recovery-001/timeline.jsonl), [closing snapshot](https://jorgefajardom-coder.github.io/NASA-GODS-EYE-/replay/recorded-recovery-001/snapshot.json), and [public rasters](https://jorgefajardom-coder.github.io/NASA-GODS-EYE-/replay/recorded-recovery-001/public_rasters.json). They preserve the recorder's internal run_id and source provenance. The loader checks snapshot/timeline closure, counts, immutable route IDs, run/schema/time/map identity, raster geometry/versions and evaluator isolation before rendering.
- [Demo run manifest](https://jorgefajardom-coder.github.io/NASA-GODS-EYE-/replay/demo/manifest.json): title, summary, disclaimer, provenance, terrain grid metadata, POIs, AI disclosure and file list.
- [Demo timeline](https://jorgefajardom-coder.github.io/NASA-GODS-EYE-/replay/demo/timeline.json) and [routes](https://jorgefajardom-coder.github.io/NASA-GODS-EYE-/replay/demo/routes.json): mission states, agent poses, events and route decisions over simulated time.
- In the running page, `window.mge.state()` returns the current replay state as JSON (time, mission state, map version, agents with pose and resources, active route, camera and layer), and `window.mge.about` repeats what is real and what is simulated.
- Private-browser, backend-off acceptance (AC-08) must be recorded for this featured package; this description does not claim that check has passed. Optional geology/context appears only for matching scene metadata. The viewer never borrows the evaluator reference or another scene's rasters.

## AI use (required declaration)

- AI tools were used and are declared in [AI_USAGE.md](https://github.com/jorgefajardom-coder/NASA-GODS-EYE-/blob/main/docs/AI_USAGE.md) and [ai_usage.json](https://github.com/jorgefajardom-coder/NASA-GODS-EYE-/blob/main/docs/ai_usage.json), with the affected files.
- The intro video (Kling) and the astronaut portrait (ChatGPT) are AI-generated and carry a visible "AI-generated" watermark. The simulated replay fixture was generated with AI-assisted code; it is not observational data.

## Optional

- [Mission checklist](https://github.com/jorgefajardom-coder/NASA-GODS-EYE-/blob/main/docs/mission_checklist.md), [requirements](https://github.com/jorgefajardom-coder/NASA-GODS-EYE-/blob/main/docs/requirements.md) and [science decisions](https://github.com/jorgefajardom-coder/NASA-GODS-EYE-/blob/main/docs/science_decisions.md).

- Optional gateway status: ?gateway=http://127.0.0.1:8010 from a local frontend with allowed CORS origin; HTTPS deployment needs a compatible HTTPS/WSS gateway. The panel validates its own source/run, recovers a fresh authoritative snapshot after reconnecting, and never feeds the 3D scene or sends goals. A connected transport is not a validated LIVE mission.
